claims.text: Applying an ultrathin conformal WC layer by ALD to W particles before Cu infiltration will improve W–Cu interfacial bonding.
Improved W–Cu interfacial bonding will reduce void formation.
Improved W–Cu interfacial bonding will reduce phase separation.
The WC-coated composite will have enhanced thermal conductivity and mechanical durability under high thermal flux and irradiation relative to direct infiltration or non-ALD vapor-coated baselines.
The proposed starting material is W particles or a connected W skeleton embedded in a Cu matrix made by conventional infiltration.
ALD can deposit an ultrathin WC coating on W particles before Cu infiltration.
The ALD step can be performed well below W's melting point and Cu's boiling point while avoiding unwanted phase changes.
Fusion-reactor W/Cu-containing components are intended to operate in high-thermal-flux environments where irradiation resistance is relevant.
The ALD process will form a uniform nanoscale WC interfacial layer.
A nanoscale WC interphase will lower interfacial free energy and improve Cu wetting on W.
A nanoscale WC interphase will inhibit void nucleation.
Reducing the surface-energy mismatch and interfacial tension between W and Cu will make Cu infiltration more uniform.
More uniform Cu infiltration will minimize voids and suppress phase separation.
Reduced void formation and phase separation will improve thermal transport and mechanical integrity under irradiation and high thermal loading.
Direct Cu infiltration and non-ALD vapor-coating approaches commonly produce localized voids and phase separation.
The intervention is applicable to W–Cu powder-metallurgy or infiltration routes processed below W's melting point and Cu's boiling point.
Prior results indicate that surface treatments can enhance interfacial bonding.
The magnitude of thermal-conductivity and mechanical-durability improvements under irradiation depends on ALD process control and subsequent processing.
An uncoated control subjected to otherwise identical infiltration, sintering, thermal cycling, and simulated irradiation can isolate the effect of the ALD WC coating.
Failure to achieve statistically lower void density, higher thermal conductivity, and comparable or better mechanical properties than the uncoated control would falsify the hypothesis.
